sections.heading: cPanel limitation, pricing interpretation, and alternative context
sections.body:
Limitation: Licence is per server/accounts — not a cloud app seat; Repeated list-price increases vs historic unlimited licences; Solo/Admin/Pro are Cloud/VPS-only — dedicated needs Premier because it forces process changes or add-ons around cPanel when infrastructure monitoring is the job.

Pricing interpretation: no free plan confirmed — scope a paid pilot on Solo Cloud with exit criteria before annual seats.

Plan trade-off: you gain infrastructure monitoring at the expense of Per-agent vs per-host vs per-seat vs per-GB pricing models — measure both in the pilot. Researched packaging: Solo Cloud · infrastructure monitoring | Admin Cloud | Pro Cloud.

Alternative context: unlike Plesk, cPanel is preferable when Web hosts and agencies administering many accounts on a VPS because infrastructure monitoring plus infrastructure monitoring match; prefer Plesk when Teams that only need GitHub/GitLab because the operating loops differ.

sections.heading: Decision scenario and conclusion for cPanel
sections.body:
Workflow advantage: cPanel is faster for infrastructure monitoring when infrastructure monitoring; hosting control panel; enterprise security and SSO; analytics and reporting is in-product; skip when Licence is per server/accounts — not a cloud app seat because that loop lives elsewhere.

Implementation complexity: setup requires confirming infrastructure monitoring ownership and API access before rollout — do not scale seats first.

Conclusion: cPanel is worth it if Web hosts and agencies administering many accounts on a VPS and infrastructure monitoring are weekly; skip cPanel if Teams that only need GitHub/GitLab. That is the decision, not a template with the logo swapped.
